correct_answer: VLAN not allowed on trunk link
why_ai_was_wrong: AI saw the VLAN was missing in 'show vlan' output but failed to check 'show interfaces trunk' where it was explicitly denied.
lesson_learned: Always check trunking configurations when dealing with cross-switch VLAN propagation issues.

why_ai_was_wrong: AI noticed clients weren't getting IPs and guessed exhaustion without checking the 'show ip dhcp pool' network mask against the interface.
lesson_learned: Verify DHCP pool network declarations strictly match the serving interface subnet.

correct_answer: DNS service not enabled on router (no ip domain-lookup)
why_ai_was_wrong: AI assumed network reachability was the issue because pings failed by hostname, but 'no ip domain-lookup' was active in the config.
lesson_learned: Check local resolver status on the device before assuming external DNS failure.

correct_answer: ACL applied inbound instead of outbound
why_ai_was_wrong: AI identified the correct ACL lines but failed to verify the direction of application on the interface.
lesson_learned: The direction (in/out) of an ACL application is as critical as the ACL rules themselves.

correct_answer: NAT inside/outside not configured on interfaces
why_ai_was_wrong: AI analyzed the NAT translations and found none, assuming pool issues without verifying interface assignments.
lesson_learned: Always verify 'ip nat inside' and 'ip nat outside' are applied to the correct interfaces.

correct_answer: WPA2-PSK passphrase mismatch between client and wireless access point
why_ai_was_wrong: AI flagged authentication method mismatch instead of checking the specific pre-shared key config on client profiles.
lesson_learned: Wireless security issues often stem from mismatched PSK passphrases even when SSID broadcast is working.

why_ai_was_wrong: AI noticed interface flapping and assumed physical disconnection, missing the high CRC error count in 'show interfaces'.
lesson_learned: Interface errors (CRC, giants, runts) are strong indicators of duplex/speed mismatches, not just cable disconnects.

correct_answer: Subnet mask mismatch on GigabitEthernet0/0 interface (configured 255.255.255.240 instead of 255.255.255.0)
why_ai_was_wrong: AI blamed basic Layer 1/2 connectivity because ping failed, missing the /28 vs /24 subnet mask conflict on the router interface.
lesson_learned: Always calculate interface network boundaries and subnet masks when ping fails to adjacent subnets.
